subject: Embedding pricing — vectors vs tokens, dims & model support
messages:
From: Thomas Wu <thomas.wu@nimbletext.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbletext.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embedding pricing — quick clarifications

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NimbleText is excited about potentially using Redwood for our vector search pipeline. Before we put together an internal budget, a few quick questions about embeddings pricing and model compatibility: 

- Do you charge per-vector or per-token for embeddings? Is there a hybrid (e.g., per-vector + per-1k-tokens) model for variable-length inputs?
- Are prices differentiated by embedding dimensionality (we’re comparing 768 vs 1536 vs 4096)? Any per-dim multipliers or flat tiers?
- Which embedding models do you currently support on the hosted API, and which ones incur the premium rate? In particular we care about small (fast) vs large (higher quality) variants.
- Do you offer volume discounts or committed-usage tiers specifically for embeddings (separate from text generation)? If so, how do you calculate breakpoints?

I’ve attached a rough monthly query estimate. Can someone send a baseline rate card we can share with finance?

Thanks —
Thomas
Head of Search
NimbleText

Attachment: NimbleText_usage_estimate_20270410.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Wu <thomas.wu@nimbletext.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding pricing — quick clarifications

Hi Thomas — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Karthik (inference/SE) to provide the baseline rate card and a few notes specific to your workload.

Quick answers at a high level:
- We publish both per-vector and per-token pricing depending on the model family and whether you use streaming/byte-pair tokenization for pre-processing. For typical text->fixed-size embedding flows we tend to surface per-vector pricing (so you can forecast by query).
- Dimension tiers: we price by dimensionality buckets (examples below) rather than charging per-dimension.
- Supported models: we have a mix of Redwood-optimized small/medium/large embedding variants — I’ll let Karthik paste a short compatibility table and call out premium models.
- Volume & commitments: yes, we offer step discounts for committed monthly vector volumes and additional contract-level discounts for annual reserved capacity. Ben will share a sample breakout.

We’ve attached the public embeddings rate card (PDF) and a small note baked for NimbleText after a quick look at your estimate. Please let us know which dimension and target latency you prefer and we’ll produce a 90-day pricing projection.

Best,
Rachel
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Embeddings_RateCard_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Thomas Wu <thomas.wu@nimbletext.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding pricing — quick clarifications

Hi Thomas — following up with a concise table and a few clarifications based on your estimate. I’m an SE on the inference side; happy to hop on a short call to validate latency assumptions.

Baseline hosted embeddings pricing (example tiers) — USD: 
- Small (fast) models — e.g., redwood-embed-1-small, optimized 768-dim: $0.00020 per vector (no token charge for normalized text inputs). Typical latency 6–12 ms / vector.
- Medium models — e.g., redwood-embed-1-medium, 1536-dim: $0.00045 per vector. Latency ~12–25 ms / vector.
- Large models — e.g., redwood-embed-1-large, 4096-dim: $0.00125 per vector. Higher memory footprint; recommended for semantic recall-sensitive use cases.

Hybrid and token-sensitive flows: if you pass variable-length chunks where we perform tokenization inside the service (e.g., combining long documents and dynamically pooling), we can bill an additional token processing surcharge for long inputs: $0.40 per 1k input tokens processed (applies only when per-request input tokens exceed 2k). For most standard short-query embeddings, customers see only the per-vector charge.

Dimension handling: we use dimensionality buckets rather than per-dimension microcharges — simpler forecasting and cheaper at scale. You can mix dims in the same account; storage/nearest-neighbor costs are independent of the per-vector inference bill.

Supported models (hosted API short list):
- redwood-embed-1-small (768) — default for high-QPS low-cost use cases
- redwood-embed-1-medium (1536) — recommended balance of cost/quality
- redwood-embed-1-large (4096) — high-quality, higher compute
- open-compat/ada-embedding (768) — compatibility shim for specific customers; billed at small-model rates unless otherwise requested

Volume discounts (examples):
- 0–5M vectors / mo: listed baseline price above
- 5–25M vectors / mo: 10% off baseline
- 25–100M vectors / mo: 20% off baseline
- >100M vectors / mo: custom enterprise rate (reserve + SLA)

Committed / reserved options: we can convert estimated monthly vectors into a reserved capacity tier with both lower unit prices and optional throughput SLAs (useful for heavy re-ranking at low latency).

Notes & next steps:
- If you share your target average vector dim (e.g., 1536) and projected monthly vectors from the attached spreadsheet, I’ll send a 90-day cost projection and an optional committed-tier proposal.
- If you need a sample SOW or 30/60/90-day ramp plan for Dedicated or Private deployments, state the required latency and dataset size and we’ll scope it.

Happy to set a quick 30-min tech + pricing sync this week — suggest Wed 11:00 PT or Thu 14:00 PT.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
